text:
178 See A Local Authority v JB [2021] UKSC 52: “It is necessary to start with the first question”. The second question
was, “Is there a clear causative nexus between the inability to make a decision as to that matter and the
impairment or disturbance in the mind or brain?”, paragraph 78.

179 15 [2020] UKEAT 0266/18/2702. The judgment relates to capacity to conduct proceedings before the
Employment Tribunal, but the principles are of broader application.
Capacity (mental)
Equal Treatment Bench Book – July 2024 (May 2025 update) 97
Evidence

13. There must be sufficient evidence (expert or lay) to displace the presumption in favour of
capacity. What evidence will be sufficient will depend on the facts of any case. Although it
is the state of mind at the time of the decision that is material, you may have to rely on the
evidence of friends and family. Evidence of conduct and actions at other times leading to the
decision in question may be relevant to show when capacity was lost.
